1. Description

 SAMI 18-21-b1 adds four updates to add new features or fix bugs.

 The definitive source for the Screening+ application - codebase,
 package distributions (including this one), and documentation - is at
 the following public Github repository:

 https://github.com/ParaxialTechnologies/SAMI-VAPALS-ELCAP

 The most up-to-date and accurate version of this file can be found at

 https://vistaexpertise.net/project/screening-plus/dist/18-21/b1/

 These instructions are for your Vista environment’s sysadmin. As
 usual, please capture the complete dialog of your install and send it
 to your Screening+ support team.

 The changes in this release are:

 1.1. Support URL override for viewing images

   Request 24-0000 (high priority): Changes were made to the DICOM
     server which necessitated the change.

   solution: Feature was added to override the URL.

   reported: Karthik (date unknown).

 1.2. Generate spreadsheets from current MSH files.

   Request 24-0000 (high priority): Implement FILECSV, which generates
     spreadsheets from the linus files that store the forms at
     Mt. Sinai.

   solution: Inserts a column called "separator". All fields left of
     the separator are in our data dictionaries, all fields to the
     right of the separator are not in the DDs but are in the form
     files at MSH.

   reported: Artit Jirapatnakul (date unknown).

 1.3. Add the X-ray form: cxform.

   Request 24-0000 (high priority): Ethiopia does a lot of their
     scanning by x-ray instead of CT, so they need a form to properly
     log the information observed in the x-rays.

   solution: Develop cxform and integrate information into database.

   reported: Rick Avila (date unknown).

 1.4. Make form changes for MSH.

   Request 24-0000 (high priority): Reports ran incorrectly.

   solution: The changes made to the intake form for MSH eliminated
     three variables and changed the meaning of another variable so
     that the report generator could not tell who was enrolled or
     active. the logic in the report generator was enhanced to work
     with either VA or MSH versions of the intake form.

   reported: Artit Jirapatnakul (date unknown).

3. Prepare for installation

 This involves creating a directory to work in, running a script to
 back up certain datafiles and web-application files, and then going
 through steps to back up M routines that will be replaced by the
 patch.


 3.1. Assume the identity of your osehra Unix user

   This step assumes you use a dzdo or sudo to do this; here the
   symbol $DEMAND will stand for whichever command you use. (Also, in
   all the command-line examples below, '$' at the beginning of the
   line represents your command-line prompt.) If your configuration is
   different, please adjust this step to match your configuration:

    $ $DEMAND su - osehra


 3.2. Prepare install directory

   If this is your first time installling this, execute the following
   commands.  They create a shell variable, and then create the work
   directory and sets it as your current directory.

    $ INDIR=~/run/in/sami/18-21/b1
    $ mkdir -p $INDIR
    $ cd $INDIR

   If you've already tried installing this once, you can use the
   following commands instead:

    $ INDIR=~/run/in/sami/18-21/b1
    $ cd $INDIR
    $ rm -rf ./sami*.{txt,kid} ./auxfiles


 3.3. Download and prepare the archive file

   You may safely download the archive file sami-18-21-b1.zip in
   advance of the actual install. In the following text, "[now]"
   represents a time stamp representing your current time, and
   "[bits/sec]" is a data rate and "[time]" is how long the file took
   to transfer (both of which vary based on the user's network
   conditions).

     $ curl -# -O 'https://vistaexpertise.net/project/screening-plus/dist/18-21/b1/sami-18-21-b1.zip'
     ######################################################################## 100.0%
     $ _

   Then unzip the archive file with the following command.

     $ unzip sami-18-21-b1.zip
     Archive:  sami-18-21-b1.zip
       ...
     $ _


 3.4. Install web-application files

    At this point, the web-application files must be installed. This
    is done with a script that backs up the affected directories
    before installing anything, then upgrades the web-application
    files.

     $ ./upgrade-auxfiles
     Backing up files to ./.aux-backup:
     [... lists of files backed up ...]
     Compressing the backup:
     [... lists of files being compressed ...]
     Cleaning up.
     Done with backup of auxiliary files.

     Updating from ./auxfiles ...
     [... lists of files being updated ...]
     Done with install.

     You may now proceed with the KIDS installation.
     $ _

    Outside the VA firewall, Screening+ systems maintain up-to-date
    clones of the official GitHub repository, and this script will
    have different output.

     $ ./upgrade-auxfiles
     Backing up files to ./.aux-backup:
     [... lists of files backed up ...]
     Compressing the backup:
     [... lists of files being compressed ...]
     Cleaning up.
     Done with backup of auxiliary files.

     Found a valid Git repository; pulling updates ...
     [... output varies ...]
     Done with install.
     $ _


 3.5. Back up M routines

   Before the installation, we also need to back up existing
   Screening+ routines that will be overwritten by this install. To do
   this, you will have to start a YottaDB, GT.M, or Cache session
   (depending on your particular installation), sign in to Vista, and
   then call the direct-mode interface ^%RO ("routine out").

   We have made efforts to display accurate instructions, but there
   are likely to be minor differences between implementations. Be sure
   to follow the correct dialog for your implementation.


  3.5.1. Enter M

    At the unix prompt, enter the M environment in direct mode, using
    the 'mumps' command on YottaDB/GT.M or the 'csession' command on Cache:

    On YottaDB/GT.M:
    ----------------
    $ mumps -dir

    >_

    On Cache:
    ---------
    $ csession vapals

    Node: vapalscache, Instance: VAPALS

    >_


  3.5.2. Sign into Vista

    At the M prompt, call Vista's direct-mode interface, enter your
    access code, and then just press return at the OPTION NAME prompt
    to return to direct mode. This sets up your authentication
    variables. Here's a sample capture of this step:

    > do ^XUP

    Setting up programmer environment
    This is a TEST account.

    Access Code: *******
    Terminal Type set to: C-VT100

    Select OPTION NAME:
    >_


  3.5.3. List of routines

    The routine names to save are listed below; you may copy the list
    and paste it at the appropriate Routine prompt. At the final
    Routine prompt, press return to indicate the list of routines is
    done.

SAMICAS2
SAMICAS3
SAMICSV
SAMICUL
SAMIDCM1
SAMIDCM2
SAMIHOM4
SAMIHUL
SAMIPAT
SAMIUR
SAMIUR2
SAMIURUL


  3.5.4. Run the backup

    Creating the routine backup file differs by implementation.

    On YottaDB/GT.M
    ---------------
    Note that routines that don't currently exist will result in the
    routine name not appearing under the input line, and won't count
    towards the number of routines. These can be safely disregarded.

    In addition to naming the routines and routine-out file, we also
    provide a Header Label and press return at the Strip comments
    prompt to accept the default of No:

     >do ^%RO

     Routine Output - Save selected routines into RO file.

     Routines: SAMICAS2
     SAMICAS2
     Current total of 1 routines.

     Routines: SAMICAS3
     SAMICAS3
     Current total of 2 routines.

     Routines: SAMICSV
     SAMICSV
     Current total of 3 routines.

     Routines: SAMICUL
     SAMICUL
     Current total of 4 routines.

     Routines: SAMIDCM1
     SAMIDCM1
     Current total of 5 routines.

     Routines: SAMIDCM2
     SAMIDCM2
     Current total of 6 routines.

     Routines: SAMIHOM4
     SAMIHOM4
     Current total of 7 routines.

     Routines: SAMIHUL
     SAMIHUL
     Current total of 8 routines.

     Routines: SAMIPAT
     SAMIPAT
     Current total of 9 routines.

     Routines: SAMIUR
     SAMIUR
     Current total of 10 routines.

     Routines: SAMIUR2
     SAMIUR2
     Current total of 11 routines.

     Routines: SAMIURUL
     SAMIURUL
     Current total of 12 routines.

     Routine:

     Output device <terminal>: /home/osehra/run/in/sami/18-21/b1/sami-18-21-b1-back.ro

     Header Label: SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21 routine backup
     Strip comments <No>?: 
     SAMICAS2  SAMICAS3  SAMICSV   SAMICUL   SAMIDCM1  SAMIDCM2
     SAMIHOM4  SAMIHUL   SAMIPAT   SAMIUR    SAMIUR2   SAMIURUL

     Total of 9279 lines in 12 routines.

     >_

    On Caché
    --------
    Note that routines that don't currently exist will result in a
    warning message (specifically, the routine name will have '[???]'
    after it, and the line [does not exist] after it). These messages
    can be safely disregarded.

    In addition to naming the routines and routine-out file, we also
    provide a Description and press return at the Parameters and
    Printer Format prompts to accept the defaults of WNS and No,
    respectively:

     >do ^%RO

     Routine output (please use %ROMF for object code output)
     Routine(s): SAMICAS2
     Routine(s): SAMICAS3
     Routine(s): SAMICSV
     Routine(s): SAMICUL
     Routine(s): SAMIDCM1
     Routine(s): SAMIDCM2
     Routine(s): SAMIHOM4
     Routine(s): SAMIHUL
     Routine(s): SAMIPAT
     Routine(s): SAMIUR
     Routine(s): SAMIUR2
     Routine(s): SAMIURUL
     Routine(s):

     Description: SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21 routine backup

     Output routines to
     Device: /home/osehra/run/in/sami/18-21/b1/sami-18-21-b1-back.ro
     Parameters? ("WNS") =>
     Printer Format? No => No
     SAMICAS2.INT    SAMICAS3.INT    SAMICSV.INT     SAMICUL.INT
     SAMIDCM1.INT    SAMIDCM2.INT    SAMIHOM4.INT    SAMIHUL.INT
     SAMIPAT.INT     SAMIUR.INT      SAMIUR2.INT     SAMIURUL.INT
     >_

    You'll remain in the M environment for the next section.


4. Main install instructions

 This consists of loading and installing the KIDS package, and
 activating the new web-application files.


  4.1. Enter the KIDS Installation menu

    At the OPTION NAME prompt, select XPD MAIN to enter the Kernel
    Installation & Distribution System main menu, and at the Select
    Kernel Installation & Distribution System ... Option prompt,
    select Installation:

     >do ^XUP

     Select OPTION NAME: XPD MAIN      Kernel Installation & Distribution System


          Edits and Distribution ...
          Utilities ...
          Installation ...
          Patch Monitor Main Menu ...

     Select Kernel Installation & Distribution System <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: Installation


        1      Load a Distribution
        2      Verify Checksums in Transport Global
        3      Print Transport Global
        4      Compare Transport Global to Current System
        5      Backup a Transport Global
        6      Install Package(s)
               Restart Install of Package(s)
               Unload a Distribution

     Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: _


  4.2. Load KIDS package

    Select option 1 and press return at the Continue prompt.

     Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: 1  Load a Distribution
     Enter a Host File: /home/osehra/run/in/sami/18-21/b1/sami-18-21-b1.kid

     KIDS Distribution saved on Jan 22, 2025@12:21:20
     Comment: Released SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21

     This Distribution contains Transport Globals for the following Package(s):
        SAMI*18.0*21

       YES

        SAMI*18.0*21
     Use INSTALL NAME: SAMI*18.0*21 to install this Distribution.

        2      Verify Checksums in Transport Global
        3      Print Transport Global
        4      Compare Transport Global to Current System
        5      Backup a Transport Global
        6      Install Package(s)
               Restart Install of Package(s)
               Unload a Distribution

     Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: _

  5.# Verify checksums

    Run the "Verify Checksums in the Transport Global" option. This
    option will let you ensure the integrity of this update in two
    ways.

    First, it will compare the routines you already have in your
    habitat to what this update was developed to replace, and if they
    don't match, it will warn you. Second, it will compare the
    routines that have been loaded from the KIDS file to what the
    developers distributed, to be sure the KIDS file was not corrupted
    in transit.

    To get a checksum report, you would select Installation option 2,
    provide the distribution name, verify that you want the routines
    listed with checksums on your screen. Here's a sample session.

    Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: 2<Enter> Verify Checksums in Transport Global
    Select INSTALL NAME: SAMI*18.0*21<Enter>     Loaded from Distribution  [datetime]
         => Released SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21  ;Created on [datetime]

    This Distribution was loaded on [datetime] with header of
       Released SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21  ;Created on [datetime]
       It consisted of the following Install(s):
       SAMI*18.0*21

    Want each Routine Listed with Checksums: Yes// <Enter>  YES
    DEVICE: HOME// ;C-SCROLL<Enter>  TELNET



    PACKAGE: SAMI*18.0*20     [datetime]                                PAGE 1
    ‍---------------------------------------------------------------------------


    [list of checksums; see below]

       <x> Routines checked, <y> failed.



       1      Load a Distribution
       2      Verify Checksums in Transport Global
       3      Print Transport Global
       4      Compare Transport Global to Current System
       5      Backup a Transport Global
       6      Install Package(s)
              Restart Install of Package(s)
              Unload a Distribution

    Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: _

    Checksums that matched will be displayed as

    RNAME     Calculated  xxxxxxxxx

    where "RNAME" is the name of the routine, and "xxxxxxxxx" is a
    checksum value.  This is normal; "RNAME" may be safely installed.
    If all of them match, the line below should say "<x> Routines
    checked, 0 failed."

    If the routine being replaced is not what was expected to be
    there, you will see something like

    RNAME     Before Checksum Calculated xxxxxxxxx expected value yyyyyyyyy

    where "xxxxxxxxx" is the checksum of the routine that's currently
    installed on your system, but "yyyyyyyyy" is what was expected to
    be there. If one of these appears, do not proceed with the
    installation until you understand why these don't match, and have
    confirmed with the Screening+ development team that it's safe to
    proceed. Otherwise, you may corrupt the Screening+ application,
    which may break certain features -- or even endanger patient
    health or privacy.

    If the routine that you're installing doesn't have a matching
    checksum, you will see something like

    RNAME     After Checksum Calculated xxxxxxxxx expected value yyyyyyyyy

    This indicates that your release has likely been corrupted
    somewhere along the line. In such cases, reach out to the
    Screening+ development team to get a clean copy of the release.

  5.1. Install KIDS package

    Select option 6, enter the space bar at the INSTALL NAME prompt,
    and press return at the next three prompts. Note that '[now]'
    denotes the current time when you're doing the install.

     Select Installation <TEST ACCOUNT> Option: 6  Install Packages(s)
     Select INSTALL NAME:    SAMI*18.0*21     Loaded from Distribution    [now]
        => Released SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21  ;Created on Jan 22, 2025@12:21:20

     This Distribution was loaded on [now] with header of
        Released SAMI*18.0*21 SEQ #21  ;Created on Jan 22, 2025@12:21:20
        It consisted of the following Install(s):
        SAMI*18.0*21
     Checking Install for Package SAMI*18.0*21

     Install Questions for SAMI*18.0*21



     Want KIDS to INHIBIT LOGONs during the install? NO//
     Want to DISABLE Scheduled Options, Menu Options, and Protocols? NO//

     Enter the Device you want to print the Install messages.
     You can queue the install by enter a 'Q' at the device prompt.
     Enter a '^' to abort the install.

     DEVICE: HOME// ;C-SCROLL  TELNET

                    [now]

                    [now]

     Install Completed
